scope: Targeted review of the seven undated releases and weight-access gaps shown by the chart. The catalog contained 28 unclassified weight records, of which 26 were dated and shown. Two records overlap the date and weight sets: 33 distinct records in total. This is not a search for all new releases.
limitations: DeepSeek Chat is dated to January 2024 at month precision from original public API rollout documentation; an exact launch day is not established.

Sonar Reasoning Pro is dated to February 2025 at month precision by inference from original before/after publisher documentation and contemporaneous release observations; no exact publisher launch-day announcement was recovered.
MiniMax M2 Her uses the named standalone public API product launch; earlier embedded use in consumer products is recorded separately.
Qwen3.8 Max Prime is excluded as a documented Fast mode serving tier of Max. Its SKU launch date remains unverified; this is not presented as a verified date.

Closed weight access means no public downloadable exact model or documented equivalent was found at review time. It is not a legal ownership assertion or a guarantee that weights will never be released.
Unrelated model attributes and all parameter audit metadata were preserved. Other missing catalog attributes, including undisclosed parameter counts, are outside this targeted audit.

This establishes the public API product release, distinct from earlier invitation-only testing and later backing-model upgrades.

results.reason: Alibaba’s exact qwen3.8-max-prime pricing row explicitly links to Fast mode (Prime). Its Chinese Prime guide says supported model capabilities and limits remain those of the original model and describes speed, billing, rate limits and mode-specific identifiers. Vercel corroborates that Prime is the high-speed edition of Max retaining its architecture and full capabilities. These sources identify a serving mode of the existing Max model, without documenting an independently trained Prime release. Exclude the serving-tier duplicate from independent-model counts while preserving its frozen audit record. This is not a claim of byte-identical deployed tensors or an exact Max-0902 snapshot mapping, and is independent of the unresolved SKU launch date.
results.date_limitation: Prime SKU launch date remains unverified. Exclusion follows its documented serving-tier identity, not a fabricated date.

release_date.evidence: January 2024 is supported at month precision by DeepSeek’s original API rollout materials: a January 11 committed Chatbox guide explicitly configures deepseek-chat at api.deepseek.com, and the January 18 native README invites API-key registration. These establish the exact alias in the initial January API rollout, independently of later V2/V3 upgrades. The precise public launch day is not established; January 30 remains a secondary retrospective claim and is not asserted.

open_weights.evidence: Closed under the user-requested availability rule: the official Weaver Alpha page exposes the hosted multi-model system but no weight source, and exact-name/public-weight/GitHub searches did not locate a downloadable Mancer Weaver checkpoint. The status does not assert ownership of constituent models or perpetual non-release.

Open weights: Microsoft’s exact MAI Code 1.1 Flash on-device GGUF is publicly downloadable through its unauthenticated Azure ML registry. Direct registry read, complete file listing and successful HEAD on the 56.3 GB model file verify actual public distribution. Official VS Code docs bind it to the named model. This establishes the released quantized variant, not byte-identical weights to the hosted full-precision backend or its separate parameter figures.

release_date.evidence: January 23, 2026 is the public release of the tracked MiniMax M2-her API product on OpenRouter, documented by the serving platform’s own release page and exact MiniMax-provider endpoint metadata. MiniMax’s January 27 technical introduction and Puter’s January 26 integration corroborate this release sequence. Earlier Q4 2025 use in MiniMax’s consumer products is a separate deployment, not this standalone public API launch.

AWS announced public availability of the exact Pixtral Large 25.02 revision on April 8, 2025, with model ID mistral.pixtral-large-2502-v1:0. This is an original release announcement for the tracked revision. The older 2411 family release does not invalidate the exact 2502 launch; no unsupported equivalence is assumed.

open_weights.evidence: Classified as closed under the tracker's availability rule: no public downloadable weights for the exact 2502 revision were found in the official Mistral inventory, native model index or exact-name public repository search. Hosted API access is documented. The downloadable 2411 checkpoint is not proven equivalent. This records current weight availability, not proprietary ownership or a permanent restriction.

release_date.evidence: February 2025 at month precision, inferred from contemporaneous original documentation and launch observations. Perplexity’s January 30 supported-model table has the non-Pro Reasoning model only; the January 31 native discussion reproduces the same list. Its February 5 table adds exact sonar-reasoning-pro. NanoGPT’s original February 3 current-release/availability announcement and the February 4 native report of the new deployment corroborate February introduction. The combined evidence supports the month, while an exact original Perplexity launch day remains unrecovered. Do not use the February 5 archive capture as a launch day or transfer the January 28/29 non-Pro announcement.
